verdict.rationale: Vast.ai documents Volumes as persistent storage that survives instance destruction and can be reattached to new instances. However, the docs describe them as "local" volumes, not network-attached storage, so portability across hosts or GPU rentals is not shown. One community comment wishes persistent disks were easier to work with, which suggests friction but does not contradict the capability. Missing for 10: evidence of network-attached storage, reattachment across different host machines, CLI/API volume workflow details, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: Volumes provide persistent storage that survives instance destruction and can be reattached to new instances.
Volumes - Persistent local storage that survives instance deletion
You will see an option labeled Local volume with a + (plus) button next to it.
The Storage page allows you to easily access and manage your volumes - storage that can be attached to your instances for data storage.
